sliceReports.summary: Slice 1 of 3 (R1 finish). I read the earlier run's work on this branch and checked it against the requirements and design. The defaults map (47 entries), the SemanticType union, the icon registry, ZestIcon, the UI/index.ts exports, the .zestIcon styles and package.json (1.7.0) already match, so I changed no production code. I ran the four slice test files (semanticTypeIcons, ZestIcon, zestIconPerformance, semanticTypeButtonConfigDefaults) with coverage off; Jest also picked up 10 more suites that match those names. All 14 suites and 163 tests pass. I did not run the full suite with coverage, the build or a bundle-size check, and I did not read the docs/guidelines files that AGENTS.md lists. The tests below prove R1: all 47 types render an icon and keep their label, the 28 new names are accepted by SemanticType, a custom registration for a new name wins, unknown or differently-cased names render a plain button, and the defaults map lists every built-in name in its original order.

sliceReports.summary: Slice 2 verified against the code. The tests, docs and code already on the branch cover R2, R4, R5, R6, R7 and R8, and all of them pass. Added one test for the one gap found, the R2 pitfall that defaults must not edit the configuration the app passes in: a deeply frozen provider config is merged with the built-in defaults, the app's override wins for 'search', 'copy' keeps its built-in look, and neither the config nor the built-in map changes. No production code was changed. Result: 18 suites, 226 tests pass when run on __tests__ only. A plain `npx jest` also picks up old scratch copies of tests under .devteam/runs/20261025-084314/scratch, and 3 of those fail; they are not project tests.

findings.description: The package is not marked "sideEffects": false (or a CSS-file list), so bundlers cannot drop unused icon code. This also weakens R5 (an app should not carry icons it never uses). Add the flag, with a CSS list because the CSS is injected.

findings.description: Several of the 28 new types are visually identical to existing ones. This is acceptable and cheap, but it is not very distinct for an 'exhaustive' set. The icon shapes follow Feather's MIT-licensed icons with no attribution recorded.

findings.description: Stronger proof would be a computed-style check or a visual check. Not blocking: the tests would notice the CSS rule being deleted or the icon stroke changing.
findings.evidence: The disabled-dimming and filled-variant tests assert on CSS source text via regex (and stroke=currentColor) because jest maps CSS to identity-obj-proxy; they would fail if the rules were removed, but not if another rule overrode them.

findings.description: Real-theme visibility is only checked structurally. Acceptable for a CSS-variable library.
